- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 3 consecutive negative values), reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to account for bearish momentum.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecasted decline, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If forecasted price is > 10% above recent 10-day average, apply downward bias of 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is significantly above true outcome, reduce forecast by 3–8% to avoid overconfidence in bullish signals.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 75% of forecast, apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to future forecasts.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, avoid large deviations — use 1–3% smoothing to prevent overfitting to recent spikes.
